sampling_model.design: A binary instrument \(Z\) randomized conditionally on finite-support \(X\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \((X,Z,D,V)\) for the finite-sample coverage theorem; identification itself is a population-law statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary received treatment \(D=D_Z\) with all four compliance types permitted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed arm-state masses \(q\) are multinomial functionals; the baseline confidence surface projects a simultaneous primitive region and does not require a smooth endpoint estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Provides partial identification and inference for treatment effects with endogenous treatment and weak sample-selection monotonicity.
Expands sharp ordinal-benefit bounds to observational settings and imperfect randomized trials.
Derives uniformly sharp bounds for marginal treatment effects among always-observed individuals in a latent-index treatment model, with tighter bounds under monotone sample selection.
Derives nonparametric average-effect bounds under sample selection and noncompliance.
Derives breakdown frontiers for average effects and the proportion benefiting under two assumption relaxations.
Derives LATE and average-effect bounds under joint relaxations of independence and monotonicity.
Constructs an output-sensitive polyhedral decomposition for sufficient-matrix multiparametric complementarity problems.
Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous optimizer over nonoverlapping regions.
Its confidence interval procedure for the fraction benefiting is pointwise consistent.
Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection confidence intervals.
Provides uniform asymptotic inference using randomly perturbed linear-program value functions.

body.tldr: Random assignment can coexist with endogenous receipt and outcomes observed only in a post-treatment selected sample. The target is the probability of strict ordinal benefit among always-selected treatment compliers when both treatment monotonicity and selection monotonicity can fail. A defier-share budget and an aggregate minority-selection budget generate an exact finite union of orientation-specific, linear-size rational threshold-cut polytopes. A reverse construction lifts every projected point to a full response law, yielding attained sharp endpoints without a uniform survivor-mass lower bound, exact pointwise computation, finite rational sensitivity charts, distinct falsification and breakdown labels, and simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage. The genuinely open computational question is an output-sensitive chart enumerator that remains complete on degenerate and lower-dimensional strata.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-complier mean and marginal-treatment-effect bounds either maintain treatment monotonicity through a no-defier or latent-index model or tighten through one-sided selection, while published ordinal-benefit bounds under imperfect compliance omit truncation by selection. Existing two-assumption breakdown frontiers do not confront a latent principal-stratum denominator that can vanish.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied model permits treatment defiers and both opposing selection responses, constrains their prevalence through two interpretable budgets, and asks for an ordinal individual-benefit probability within the always-selected complier stratum.
project_justification.fill: The exact projection-and-lifting theorem reduces the compatible full laws to orientation-indexed threshold-cut polytopes of linear extended size. The induced endpoint and frontier theorems give a complete two-budget robustness object with certificates and finite-sample outer coverage.

body.related_work: Dong and Heiler (2026) provide the closest setup and writing model: assignment affects endogenous receipt, outcomes are selected, and the intensive-margin complier population is substantively examined in Job Corps and Oregon. Their sharp target is a mean under treatment monotonicity and covariate-dependent one-sided selection, so their trimming construction informs but does not subsume the joint-violation ordinal ratio. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) provide the closest identification technique for strict ordinal benefit: finite response functions and symbolic sharp optimization. Their framework has no post-treatment selection variable or selection-defined principal stratum; their Discussion instead identifies bootstrap inference and efficient incorporation of continuous covariates as extensions. Bartalotti, Kédagni, and Possebom (2023) derive uniformly sharp marginal-treatment-effect bounds for always-observed individuals under a latent-index treatment model. Their latent-index treatment rule excludes treatment defiers, while their tighter monotone-sample-selection result excludes the within-cell opposing selection responses permitted by the minority budget here. Chen and Flores (2015) jointly analyze noncompliance and sample selection for always-employed complier means under monotonicity and mean dominance. Masten and Poirier (2020) motivate a complete two-assumption conclusion-first chart; Picchetti (2026) shows how a defier-share coordinate enters an IV breakdown analysis. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones (2009) and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski (2007) inform the adjacency and lexicographic-degeneracy handle, but their output objects differ from unperturbed disjunctive rational endpoint charts. Huang et al. (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Cho and Russell (2024) inform constrained and projection inference; the proposed baseline guarantee is instead a conservative finite-sample projection of one simultaneous multinomial region.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve evidence supports finite exact all-bases chart enumeration but not output-sensitive complexity. The early kill test must reproduce the explicit binary surface \(L(d,s)=\max\{0,(0.05-d-s(0.20+d))/(0.15+d-s(0.20+d))\}\) and \(U(d,s)=(0.05+d)/\max\{0.10,0.15-s(0.20+d)\}\) on \(d\in[0,0.05]\), \(s\in[0,1/2]\), together with the opposite-orientation witness and a vanishing-denominator example. It must emit equality strata, empty-target labels, endpoint full-law certificates, and an audit showing that rejected bases do not hide exponential work. Failure triggers a computational-kernel pivot; it does not invalidate the projection theorem or pointwise endpoint algorithm.
body.honest_scope: The projection, sharpness, connectedness, sparse-attainment, finite-chart, frontier, and coverage claims are theorem obligations, not established results. The output-sensitive enumerator is deliberately exposed as the first-class open question. No strongly polynomial algorithm, polynomial bound on the number of orientations or charts, root-\(n\) regular endpoint inference at ties, or empirical reanalysis is claimed. Under complete selection and zero budgets, the target reduces to the known ordinal complier-benefit bounds.
